Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

however adverb

no matter how

also no matter how, however much, in whatever way, however you like

classical

Cic. Tusc. 2.13: ager quamvīs fertilis
Cic. Sen. 67: quamvīs sit adulēscēns
Mart. 13.81.1

quamvīs

adverb with an adjective or adverb; conjunction with the subjunctive, “however much, although”

however (much), however + adjective

The main clause often answers with tamen.

Examples

  • quamvīs lāta gerat patella rhombum, rhombus lātior est tamen patellā

    however wide the dish that holds the turbot, the turbot is wider than the dishMart. 13.81

  • utcumque erit, juvābit tamen

    however it turns out, I shall still be glad of itLiv. praef. 3

  • quōquō modō potes ad mē fac veniās

    however you can, make sure you come to meCic. Fam. 14.4.3

Other words

  • utcumque — however, in whatever way

    adverb · also used · classical · Liv. praef. 3: utcumque erit, juvābit tamen

  • quōquō modō — in whatever way, however (one can)

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.4.3: quōquō modō potes ad mē fac veniās

  • quamlibet — however much, as much as you like

    adverb · also used · classical · Quint. 1.1.18: quamlibet parum sit (Lewis & Short); Phaedr. 1.25.6: quamlibet lambe ōtiō

    Chiefly poetry and post-Augustan prose.

See also however.
